headline: The faintest supernova ever observed refuses to go out, staying visible for nearly a year
summary: An international team of astronomers, including Paul Groot of Radboud University, has discovered that a supernova explosion does not always have to be extremely bright. The team has identified the faintest supernova observed to date. It remained visible for an exceptionally long time and appears to have been caused by a so-called white dwarf and a relatively small companion star. The discovery may have implications for our understanding of the evolution of binary stars and the measurement of the expansion of the universe. The results were published in Nature Astronomy.

headline: The first flash of a dying star can reveal its hidden surroundings

That fleeting moment offers an unusually direct glimpse of the star at the instant of destruction. But what if the light has to fight its way through a cloud of gas the star expelled before dying?
